lines.text: Airbnb open-sourced Skipper, which lets a program pick up where it left off after a crash.
Some jobs have many steps, wait for people, or call other services. A restart halfway is a problem.
lines.title: The problem

lines.text: Many tools use a separate central service. Airbnb wanted each service to own its workflows and database.
lines.title: Where it runs

lines.text: A workflow is just a Java or Kotlin class. Each action's result is saved as a checkpoint.
lines.title: How it works

lines.text: After a crash, the workflow runs again from the top. Finished actions just return their saved results.
lines.title: Recovery

lines.text: Actions must be safe to repeat, because a crash can happen before a checkpoint is saved.
lines.title: The catch

lines.text: Skipper is now open source under Apache 2.0. The team owns database load and recovery.
lines.title: Takeaways
